title: Karla Sofía Gascón Reflects on Emilia Pérez Oscar Backlash and New Roles
excerpt:
Karla Sofía Gascón revisited the controversy around her historic Oscar campaign.
Speaking at India's film festival, she also discussed Trinidad, Las Malas and her acting career.
body_md:
Karla Sofía Gascón has revisited the controversy that surrounded her awards campaign for Emilia Pérez in an interview at the International Film Festival of India in Goa. Her performance made her the first transgender performer nominated for an acting Oscar, but the achievement was overshadowed by intense debate about past social-media posts.

Gascón argued that some of the hostility came from people unwilling to see someone like her receive a major award. She also disputed the public portrait of her that emerged during the controversy. Those statements represent the actor's account of events, rather than an independent resolution of the competing claims about the posts and the ensuing backlash.

The actor described lengthy awards campaigns as difficult experiences in which artistic achievement can become entangled with political and economic interests. She said she would prefer to focus on acting and allow audiences to decide what they think of the work. Gascón also voiced concern about what she sees as a regression in transgender rights and protections for sexual diversity.

Her work in Jacques Audiard's Emilia Pérez brought major recognition, including acting honors associated with the Cannes Film Festival, the European Film Awards and the Lumière Awards, alongside Golden Globe and BAFTA nominations. Gascón said one significant professional change is that she no longer needs to audition for every part, after a career stretching back more than three decades.

At the festival she was presenting the Spanish Western Trinidad, which had its world premiere in Goa. She plays a gun-carrying antagonist who uses a wheelchair. Gascón recalled initially imagining the familiar horseback-riding and shooting opportunities of a Western, only to discover that the role would require a very different physical approach. She said that challenge became an opportunity to consider other people's experiences.

She also discussed Las Malas, Armando Bo's adaptation of Camila Sosa Villada's novel, in which she portrays Tía Encarna. Filming took place in Argentina and Uruguay, and Gascón described the role as one of the strongest experiences of her career. She raised the possibility of a future Cannes or Venice appearance, but did not announce a confirmed premiere date.

Elsewhere in the conversation, Gascón praised Audiard for giving performers creative freedom and emphasized the value of working across languages and national borders. The interview offered a fuller picture of how she interprets the past year's controversy and where she hopes to take her career next, rather than announcing any new Oscar-related development.

seo_description: Karla Sofía Gascón discusses her Emilia Pérez Oscar backlash, transgender rights, Trinidad and Las Malas at India's film festival.
